issues.evidence: R12 (0 ohm, R_NOINSTALL) and C7 (47pF, C_NOINSTALL) are drawn as NOINSTALL but the symbol instances have (in_bom yes) (dnp no), so they appear in the BOM/CPL and the netlist carries no DNP mark. R12 bridges /RXD (Q2 drain, R9 4.7k to +12V, U3 RIN) to /SEATALK1 (Q2 gate, Q1 drain, MK5).
issues.why_it_matters: An assembler working from the BOM fits R12, which ties Q2 drain to its own gate: Q2 becomes diode-connected on the SeaTalk bus and clamps the shared bus near Vgs(th) via R9, corrupting the bus for every instrument. C7 fitted is mostly harmless (feed-forward cap) but is still an unintended placement.
issues.time_or_money: functional risk; set DNP attribute on 2 parts

issues.evidence: +12V from the SeaTalk harness pads MK1/MK7 goes straight to U1 (AP62300) VIN pin 3 with only C6 10uF; no fuse, no reverse-polarity diode/FET, no TVS on +12V.
issues.why_it_matters: Marine 12V bus sees 14.4V+ charging and load-dump/inductive transients; AP62300 is rated 18V operating. A reversed or spiking harness destroys U1 and the 3V3 rail.
issues.time_or_money: functional risk; ~$0.15 for SMBJ18A + series Schottky/PFET

issues.evidence: U1 MPN field AP62300WU-7 but Digikey PN field is 31-AP62200TWU-7TR-ND (an AP62200T part).
issues.why_it_matters: Ordering by the distributor PN gets a different (lower-current / different variant) regulator than the MPN and symbol.

issues.evidence: /SEATALK1 from MK5 goes directly to Q2 gate (pin 1) and Q1 drain with no series resistor, clamp or TVS.
issues.why_it_matters: 2N7002 Vgs max is +/-20V; bus transients or miswiring to the 12V supply with spikes can punch through the gate oxide. A 1k series R plus a zener/TVS is cheap insurance.

issues.evidence: All passives, L1 and D1 have MFG/MPN/Voltage/Dielectric/Tolerance = N/A; ratings only given by the sheet note (6.3V min caps, C6 25V min).
issues.why_it_matters: L1 saturation current and C6 voltage/dielectric are not pinned; procurement can substitute an under-rated inductor for a 3A buck.

issues.evidence: MAX3221 (RS-232 transceiver with 4 charge-pump caps) is used only to drive Q1 gate (DOUT) and to sense the Q2 drain node (RIN).
issues.why_it_matters: A logic-level FET driven straight from GPIO14 and a resistor divider/second FET on the receive side do the same job; the MAX3221 + 4 caps cost ~$1.5 and board area. It does give clean gate drive and +/-25V input tolerance, so this is optional.

acceptable_designs.reason: ESP-12E flash SPI pins are used by the module's internal flash and must be left unconnected; all carry no-connect flags.
Spare GPIO/ADC deliberately unused, flagged no-connect.
INVALID is a status output; leaving it open is fine.
MAX3221 FORCEON and ~FORCEOFF tied to VCC and ~EN tied to GND keep the transceiver permanently on and receiver enabled - intended.
ESP-12E CH_PD tied directly to +3V3 is a valid always-enabled configuration.
ESP8266 EXT_RSTB has an internal pull-up; R11 1k to GPIO16 is the standard deep-sleep wake link and limits current when SW1 is pressed while GPIO16 drives high.
GPIO2 pulled up, GPIO15 pulled down, GPIO0 pulled up with SW2 to GND - correct ESP8266 boot strapping.
SeaTalk1 is an open-collector bus pulled up inside the existing instruments; the bridge only pulls low (Q1) and senses (Q2).
R8 1k isolates MAX3221 ROUT so a programmer on MK4 can override RXD for flashing.
Q1 gate driven by MAX3221 DOUT (+/-5.5V) is within 2N7002 Vgs rating; DOUT is always actively driven (FORCEON high, DIN internal pull-up) so no gate pull-down is needed, and Q1 stays off at boot.
ESP-12E module carries its own decoupling; board adds 2x22uF + 1uF + 0.1uF on +3V3.

notes: Seatalk1 bridge: AP62300 buck 12V->3.3V (FB 75k/24k = 3.30V), ESP-12E, MAX3221 used as inverting level shifter; TX = GPIO14 -> DIN -> DOUT -> Q1 open-drain on bus (non-inverting overall), RX = bus -> Q2 inverter (R9 to 12V) -> RIN -> ROUT -> R8 -> RXD (non-inverting). Polarity and boot straps verified. Connections are via test pads (MK*), no real connector. Not assessed: AP62300 EN abs-max vs R10 pull-up to +12V (datasheet not checked), L1 Isat, layout.
